summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p cord blood transplant, chronic GVHD, steroid-induced diabetes, and dilated cardiomyopathy, was admitted for a persistent cough of one week’s duration. He had mild fatigue and increased oxygen use at rest but no fever or dyspnea. Initial chest X-ray showed no acute process. CT chest revealed new bronchial wall thickening, mucus plugging, and ground-glass opacities, more consistent with infection than GVHD flare. Respiratory viral panel and blood cultures were negative. He was treated with levofloxacin and continued on home immunosuppressants without steroid escalation. IVIG was administered as part of his scheduled therapy. His symptoms improved, oxygen requirements decreased, and he was discharged home with a short course of oral antibiotics and allopurinol for elevated uric acid. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and a new primary care provider.
